step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Nextcaller's VeraCall phone fraud detection pipeline on AWS. In the primary request flow (Flow 0), incoming telephony SIP call metadata is sent JSON-encoded via API Gateway. API Gateway invokes a Custom Authorizer Lambda function, which queries DynamoDB to validate customer credentials and API keys. Upon successful authorization, the request moves to the main VeraCall Lambda function, which calls an Amazon SageMaker inference endpoint to compute a fraud prediction score in real time (~110ms turnaround) and returns the result back through API Gateway. In the asynchronous data processing flow (Flow 1), the VeraCall Lambda function puts call metadata into an SQS queue, which persists it into an encrypted S3 bucket. Data scientists then use SageMaker Jupyter notebooks and training jobs to fetch data from S3 and retrain the machine learning models.
